# routeur_api_key (Resource)

A gateway API key (`sk-r-…`) for `api.routeur.ai`, in one project of a workspace. The secret is returned only when the key is created, so it is kept in state: protect your state accordingly. Destroying the resource revokes and deletes the key; the gateway refuses it once the change propagates.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "routeur_workspace" "payments" {
  slug = "payments"
  name = "Payments"
}

resource "routeur_project" "checkout" {
  workspace_id = routeur_workspace.payments.id
  slug         = "checkout"
  name         = "Checkout"
}

# A gateway key for the checkout service. Changing rotation_triggers
# replaces the key; create_before_destroy keeps the old one working until
# the new one exists.
resource "routeur_api_key" "checkout" {
  workspace_id = routeur_workspace.payments.id
  project_id   = routeur_project.checkout.id
  name         = "Checkout service"

  rotation_triggers = {
    rotated = "2026-10"
  }

  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}

# The secret is only returned when the key is created; hand it to the
# service, e.g. through a secret manager.
output "checkout_routeur_key" {
  value     = routeur_api_key.checkout.secret
  sensitive = true
}

# A key kept but switched off: the gateway refuses it until re-enabled.
resource "routeur_api_key" "legacy" {
  workspace_id = routeur_workspace.payments.id
  name         = "Legacy batch"
  enabled      = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name, 1–80 characters, without leading or trailing whitespace. Renaming keeps the secret.
- `workspace_id` (String) Id of the workspace this belongs to (`ws_…`), e.g. `routeur_workspace.example.id`. The `routeur_workspace` data source resolves a slug to its id. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the gateway accepts the key. Defaults to `true`; `false` disables it reversibly (the secret is kept), and removing the argument enables it again.
- `project_id` (String) Id of the project the key belongs to (`proj_…`), in the same workspace. Omitted at creation, the key goes to the workspace's default project (removing the argument later leaves the key where it is). Changing it moves the key in place; the secret is unchanged.
- `rotation_triggers` (Map of String) Arbitrary map of values that, when changed, rotate the key: Terraform replaces it with a new key (new id and secret) and deletes the old one. Add `lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }` to create the new key before the old one stops working. Caveat: Terraform applies `create_before_destroy` to everything the key depends on as well, so replacing the key's workspace or project then creates the new one first — which fails while the old one still holds its slug (workspace slugs are unique per organisation, and so are project slugs). Change such a slug in its own apply, or drop `create_before_destroy` for that apply. After `terraform import` (when no triggers are stored yet), adding `rotation_triggers` stores them without replacing the key; only a later change rotates it.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When it was created (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `disabled_at` (String) When the key was disabled (RFC 3339, UTC); null unless disabled.
- `fingerprint` (String) Display form of the key, e.g. `sk-r-…abcd`. Safe to show; never reveals the secret.
- `id` (String) Public id of the API key (`key_…`). A new key, after rotation or replacement, has a new id.
- `revoked_at` (String) When the key was revoked (RFC 3339, UTC); null unless revoked.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) The key itself (`sk-r-…`), to send to `api.routeur.ai`. Returned by the API only at creation, so it is null after `terraform import`. Sensitive.
- `state` (String) `active`, `disabled` or `revoked`; new states may be added. A key revoked outside Terraform cannot be used again, so the next plan replaces it.
- `updated_at` (String) When it was last changed (RFC 3339, UTC).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# id: <workspace_id>/<api_key_id>. The secret cannot be read back, so it
# is null after import.
import {
  to = routeur_api_key.checkout
  id = "ws_3/key_12"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <workspace_id>/<api_key_id>. The secret cannot be read back, so it is
# null after import.
terraform import routeur_api_key.checkout ws_3/key_12
```
